sections.text: Introduction

This
document details the major maintenance procedure activities 
P2, which must be performed
every 12-16 years basis or every 2000 times
operation Y12:16 as indicated at the above
title block.

The 
first draft initiated by eng. Mohamed Khames Taha Sues 500, Canal west zone.

Safety 
Precautions

items: A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,
Isolate the CB and earth both sides

Discharge the
 closing spring

Disconnect
 supply and motor voltage

Discharge the
 SF6 GAS to atmospheric pressure

Comply with
 the relevant safety regulations

Personal
 protective equipment must be used ( breathing - mask - helmet - safety shoes
 .. etc)

sections.text: Instructions for Maintenance

Life of the 
Breaker

Some points that secure a long life can be named:
 a) The burning off of the arcing 
contacts is small, 
 b) Every breaking units is supplied 
with drying agent that at least meets the life of the breaker, 
 c) The bearings in the gas filled 
space are maintenance free,
 d) The sealing of the flanges are 
achieved by double O rings.

Note: The first cause to open a breaking element is 
with one of:
 a) Heavy burnt arcing 
contacts,
 b) Ascertained leakage of 
SF6 gas,
 c) Ascertained mechanical 
failure.
Life of contacts

The 
diagram below shows the number of interruptions as function of the breaking 
current that the Teflon parts of a HPL breakers can withstand before they have 
to be changed.
Number of Interruptions

Number of interruptions between two revisions at 
different breaking current levels.

ex : The breaker manages 20 interruptions at 40ka 
breaking current.

For a by bass switch a normal life of contacts and 
Teflon parts is 2000 operations.
External Cleaning

All the 
HPL breakers are (wash proof) and can be cleaned by means of rising with water 
without damaging vital parts.
Lubrication

The bearing of the breaker not need 1ubrication 
before the general overhaul.

Plain bearing in mechanism detail as (arms, links 
and link gears) and the teeth of gears will be painted on in a thin layer of 
(grease G)
Check of dashpots oil is necessary.

sections.text: Treatment of Contact Surfaces

When 
breaking elements are dismantled, the contact shall be treated as follows.
Silvered Surfaces

Shall be 
cleaned with soft cloth and solvent (trichloroethane)
Copper Surfaces

Shall 
cleaned with soft cloth and solvent (trichloroethane).
Aluminum Surfaces

Cleaned 
with emery cloth or steel brush and coated with thin layer of Vaseline
Treatment of gaskets and seating surfaces
With reassemble of the breaker all gaskets shall be replaced by new one.
The sealing surfaces of the flanges are coated with corrosion preventing agent.
Material for degreasing and cleaning trichloroethane (art. no 11771016-611)

Material for greasing of O-rings and nitrite rubber in static sealing (ABB 
grease G or Aero shall grease 22, Mobil grease 28)

Material for rust protection of phosphatized steel Valvoline tedyle 506(art no. 
1241 Doll-108)
Material for the solution of contact glue (Acetone)

sections.text: Instruction for gas filling

After overhaul or repair of the breaker, it shall 
be filled with SF6 gas as follows:

Evacuate till a pressure of (1-m bar) and continue 
with pumping at last (1 hour) from the moment the pressure of (1-m bar) is 
reached.

Stop the evacuation and fill the breaker with dry 
and clean nitrogen up till atmospheric pressure

Evacuate again to a pressure (1-m bar) and fill the 
breaker with clean SF6 gas to the normal working pressure. (Or to storing 
pressure 0.25 bar)

items:
Prior to
 dismounting the function values of the CB should be checked and recorded
Measure the resistance of the main contact

Measure the operating times (C - O
 - CO)

Check
 of the SF6 GAS quality

Empty the SF6 
 gas of the
 CB to the atmosphere pressure,

Dismount the breaking unit and 
 place it on appropriate
 transport base

Transport the breaking unit to the work shop for the
 overhaul

Place the breaking unit on the mounting device
 ( special tool ) and connect their mechanism together,

Dismount the (capacitors - top covers - 
 desicants
 container - upper current collector with upper terminal flange),
Dismount breaking units isolator carefully,

Dismount the lower current collector 
 & take out the
 puffer,

The main components of the breaker pole will now be
 accessible for cleaning, inspection and replace the
 burnt or damaged parts.

Replace the 
 contacts set and nozzles when
 the fixed breaking contacts ( arc contact ) has been burned down max 
 (3 MM.) or hard burned
 on the outer diameter. as shown below:

Normally only replace meant of the fixed
 arc contact
 is required (using special tool) if more, carefully cleaning or replacement of the contacts fingers
 (main contacts) should be required

Grease the are and main contacts with (Grease K) and
 remount in reveres order

Replace the 
 following parts nozzle,
 sleeve, contacts, springs, and breaking contact. These parts and contact sets are delivered in composed
 parts mounted together.

Treat and contact surface, puffer contact and puffer 
 cylinder and lubricate with thin layer of (grease K) and assemble all part and remount in reverse order.

No
 lubricantion of the mechanism IS required AS all
 the bearings have teflon-coated bushes.
 The upper mechanism 
 with the piston for the puffer does
 not need to be dismounted if it is not severely polluted by waste products

If the mechanism 
 is dismounted the following parts
 should replaced

All O-rings
 replaced and lubricated

Teflon bands
 for piston and checking of piston valve is level and
 easily movable
Mount all parts IN reverse order of dismounting.

Check alignment of the fixed & moving contact by operate the puffer slowly
towards the closed position.
 After place the breaking unit In closed position by mounting device making a 
 vacuum & refill with SF6 gas

Check with A 
 snuffer
 or soapy water or { using GAS detector ) the leakage of
SF 6 GAS.
Empty the SF 6 GAS to the transport press (0.125 MP)

Place the unit in the tighten position & fix the mechanism in this
position
Repeat all the above procedure for each pole

Timing operation of the
 CB (C-O-OCO)

Main contact resistance (micro
 ohm )
Spring charging time (15 sec)
Operating voltage ( MAX & MIN ) of the ( On / Off ) coils

After carrying 
 the tests put the circuit breaker into service
 Noting the operating signs of
CB (on and off ) should be accommodated with
normal operating position
